## Citation

Jaworski, D.M., Beem-Miller, M., Lluri, G., & Barrantes-Reynolds, R. (2007). Potential Regulatory Relationship Between the Nested Gene DDC8 and Its Host Gene Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase-2. *Physiological Genomics*, 28(2), 168-178.

## Abstract

Gene nesting, where one gene is located within the intron of another, represents an interesting regulatory relationship. This study investigates the potential co-regulation of the nested gene DDC8 and its host gene TIMP-2, which encodes a tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinases.

## Key Findings

- DDC8 is nested within an intron of the TIMP-2 gene
- Analysis suggests potential co-regulation mechanisms
- Examination of promoter and regulatory elements
- Discussion of functional implications for nested gene regulation
- Insights into evolutionary conservation of this genetic arrangement

## Role

As a co-author, I contributed to bioinformatics analysis and genomic sequence examination.
